patch.objective: Validate constructor arguments, raise on bad input, and avoid mutable default parameters
secondaryObjectives: Design isolated unit tests with typical, boundary and invalid inputs and check results with assertions

sources.cite: Python Institute, PCAP-31-04 exam syllabus (revised November 2, 2026)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: Object-Oriented Programming 28.5%; objective 4.6.2 'Explain why mutable default arguments (e.g., lists, dicts) should not be passed as initializer parameters'; 6.1.1 'Interpret passed and failed tests, and rerun relevant tests after code changes to detect regressions'. The case's function is a plain function rather than an __init__; the pitfall and the fix (None, then a new object inside) are the same for an initializer.

sources.cite: Python 3.15 documentation, The Python Tutorial, 4.9.1 Default Argument Values (not re-read for this round)
sources.note: To verify: the tutorial's warning that 'The default value is evaluated only once', so a mutable default such as a list accumulates across calls, and its 'if L is None: L = []' pattern, are the standard statement of the pitfall; that section did not appear in a search for this round and was not opened. Every behavior in the case follows from defaults being evaluated once, when the def statement runs.
